abstract: Adopt space time spreading, superimposed training sequences and space-time coding to obtain a closed-form of average error probability upper bound and maximum likelihood estimation expression for multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) correlated frequency-selective channel in the presence of interference(co-channel interference and jamming signals). Moreover, the correlation at both ends of the wireless link can be incorporated equivalently into correlation at the transmit end is derived. The simulation results are presented to validate the proposed analysis.

articleTitle: A NBI suppression approach based on space-domain DBF processing for wideband MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Bandwidth is an important parameter in signal processing. A novel method for estimating the bandwidth using the linear phase relationship between two-channel narrowband signals is proposed. The two-channel model is based on the time-difference of arrival (TDOA) estimator. The second channel signal is a time delay copy of the first channel. The comparison between the proposed method and the general ones is presented. It is shown that the method is effective for signals corrupted by strong interference even at low SNR.

articleTitle: Reliability-based data-puncturing hybrid ARQ scheme with LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We propose an improved data-puncturing hybrid-ARQ scheme for Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes based on codeword reliability. Incremental redundancy is generated from punctured versions of the original data using the same encoder/decoder pair. Retransmission packet sizes are determined adaptively according to the reliability level of the decoded data. We conduct detailed simulation experiments and compare the proposed scheme with RB-HARQ and DP-HARQ approaches. The RB-DP-HARQ scheme reduces the retransmission times and the feedback channel traffic for NACK signaling with negligible overhead.

articleTitle: An new dynamic framed slotted ALOHA algorithm for RFID
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In RFID systems, in order to resolve the collision problem, ALOHA and framed slotted ALOHA algorithm have been used, but their performance are not more evident. In this paper, a new dynamic framed slotted ALOHA algorithm is presented. Simulated on Matlab, the result shows that the new algorithm is more efficiency.

articleTitle: An Isolation-Based Circuit Design for Soft Error Suppression
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: As the feature size of integrated circuits continues to shrink, deep sub-micro circuits are more susceptible to soft errors. In this paper, we propose a novel circuit design scheme, which can help increase the soft error immunity of sequential logics (such as SRAM cell and latch). The principle of the proposed circuit design is to build flexible isolation between soft-error sensitive nodes. The proposed scheme is applied to the design of various sequential logics at 70 nm technology. The simulation results show that the critical charge (the minimum charge to cause soft errors) can be increased by 1.98 times on average. Furthermore, combining together with multiple-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> (MVT), multi-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf>, and sizing techniques, the improvement of critical charge can add up to 237 times on average.

articleTitle: Designing high-efficiency class-E LDMOS power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Multifunctional RF front ends need to transmit different types of signals while maintaining efficiency and signal quality. we show that switched mode class-E power amplifiers can achieve high efficiency at RF frequency. In this paper, a 20W class-E power amplifier has been designed using MRF21030. The input match network and output network has been simulated carefully and the output efficiency of power amplifier is 63%. Further more, the effect of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dd</inf> and input power have also been analyzed.

articleTitle: Multicast routing in WDM networks with sparse light splitting
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: As multicast applications become widely popular, supporting multicast in all-optical wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) networks becomes an important problem. In this paper, we study multicast routing in sparse splitting WDM networks, in which only a small percentage of nodes are capable of light splitting. Specifically, an efficient sparse splitting constrained multicast routing algorithm called MCNFH is proposed and evaluated by simulations. The results show that the proposed algorithm has better performance in terms of wavelength channel cost and the maximum number of wavelengths per link than existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparisons between different concatenated codes impact on performance of optical CDMA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a method using alterable concatenated code to pre-encode is presented to reduce the impact of system impairment and multiple access interference (MAI) in optical code division multiple access (OCDMA) system, and comprehensive comparisons between different concatenated code type and forward error correcting (FEC) scheme are studied by simulation. In the scheme, we apply concatenated coding to the embedded modulation scheme, and optical orthogonal code (OOC) is employed as address sequence code, an avalanche photodiode (APD) is selected as the system receiver. From numerical results, we can show that the proposed system has good performance at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> with a gain of 6.4 dB improvement achieved using the concatenated code as the pre-code.

articleTitle: A nested multistage adaptive beamformer for wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A multistage adaptive beamformer for wireless communications is proposed. The beamformer adopts a novel nested system architecture to reduce the system complexity and to achieve the system optimization which is carried out independently at each stage. It is shown that this method attains an improved performance in comparison to another competitive method.

articleTitle: Impact of relay location to SER performance with different power allocation methods in cooperative system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new independent distributed sources model is proposed. The Jacobi-Anger (JA) series expansion technique is used in model establishment. Without relating to the spatial angular spread, the model error is only decided by the series order. With high order of JA series, the error can be limited to a very small range. As being generally regarded as composing of several symmetric distributions, the non-symmetric distribution in our model can be viewed as a combination of two Gaussian distributions, the ratio between which determines the shape of the non-symmetric distribution. The proposed model breaks the limitations of the small spatial angular spread and symmetric distribution in traditional distribution sources models. A new DOA estimation method is derived from the incorporation of our model into the steepest descent algorithm. Computer simulation results demonstrate that the novel model is effective and the performance of DOA estimation method is close to that of the CRB.

articleTitle: Partner choice based on beam search in wireless cooperative networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Cooperative diversity has recently emerged as an effective form of providing gains in slow fading wireless environments. In this paper, we propose a novel partner choice protocol which first selects the best relay from cooperative region consisting of n available relays and then uses this best relay for cooperation between the source and the destination. We improve the agility of this protocol by guiding the search heuristically so that as few available relays as possible are expanded during the partner choice process. We use amplify-and-forward as relaying schemes to illustrate the validity of the cooperative communication in the mobile wireless networks.

articleTitle: Modelling and simulation of digital channelized receiver based on IDFT poly-phase filter architecture
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an efficient architecture of digital channelized receiver based on IDFT poly-phase filter bank. The proposed architecture has broadband instantaneous frequency coverage, small amounts of calculation, high frequency resolution, and strong capability to distinguish simultaneous signals. This architecture also provides a good model for accurate instantaneous frequency measurement. The simulation results by Matlab indicate that it is highly efficient.

articleTitle: Sigma Delta Modulator Design Automation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Sigma delta modulator design automation from system to circuit is presented in this paper. The sigma delta modulator design flow is separated into the system and circuit level design. It often adopts Matlab Simulink for the system level design and utilizes circuit simulator Spectre for the circuit level design. We propose a methodology which is realized by a script language PERL to control and link all these simulation tools. For the purpose of the automation, we also applied simulated annealing algorithm to optimize the system parameters in the script. We have successfully implemented this automation flow for the switched-cap third-order feedback single loop single bit with the simulated annealing algorithm. The designer of the SDM is complete within one day and shows the SNDR up to 87 dB. Besides, this methodology can be applied to any architecture of the sigma delta modulators only if the system is modeled well in the behavior model.

articleTitle: Geometry and System Aspects of Spaceborne/Airborne Hybrid Bistatic SAR
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Spaceborne/airborne hybrid bi-static SAR is a new kind of remote sensor raised in recent years, whose development is still at an early stage for its great difficulty. Due to the high differences between satellites' and aircrafts' velocities and altitudes, there are remarkable differences between the hybrid system and systems which have the symmetrical structure, such as spaceborne bi-static SAR and airborne bi-static SAR. Three basic and critical issues in the hybrid system are discussed, including geometry, Doppler properties and signal model. On the basis of the research work done in this paper, imaging algorithm of the hybrid system can be further designed in the next step.

articleTitle: Effect of reference point on performance of Multidimensional Scaling algorithm for localization in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In case of time-of-arrival (TOA) measurements errors, selecting different reference point usually yields different accuracy of localization in wireless sensor networks by using classical Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) algorithm. In this paper, we derive the MDS algorithm which using centroid of network nodes as reference point, compared with which using one of nodes of sensor networks as reference point. Simulation results show that using centroid of network nodes as reference point yields better performance.

articleTitle: PiFF: A formal framework for dynamic service composition
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Service choreography and orchestration are two views of the service compositions. In order to select and compose services correctly, some formal methods and tools are used to model and verify those compositions. Pi calculus is a major theory of process algebra that can be used as the formal basis of service composition. According to analysis result of WS CDL and WS BPEL, PiFF - a formal verification framework based on pi calculus is proposed which can be used to check and validate service composition both from global and local point of views. PiFF constitutes of three parts: mapping, methods and tools. This framework can promise consistency between WS CDL and WS BPEL and guarantee developing of dynamic service composition correctly by concept of weak bisimulation.

articleTitle: A Sensorless Drive Method for Switched Reluctance Motor Based on Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The measurement of rotor position for switched reluctance drive is essential to proper running. This paper introduces a method of detecting the rotor position based on fuzzy logic. In order to improve the measurement accuracy of the rotor position, some unique techniques are adopted. First, an optimized fuzzy model of the motor is created using an Adaptive Neural Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). Secondly, the block of angle position selector and predictive filter are used. Position selector can modify the rotor-position, and predictive filter is used to examine and eliminate the noise of the feedback signal. The result of simulation indicates that the position obtained by this method is accurate for the operation of SRM.

articleTitle: Time-spreading and wavelength-group-hopping codes implemented over fiber-to-the-home networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Exploiting the inherent cyclic and periodic free-spectral-range (FSR) properties of arrayed-waveguide-grating (AWG) routers, the time-spreading and free-spectral-range (FSR) group hopping code, which embedded maximum length sequence (i.e., called TS/GH embedded M-sequence code) is configured over fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) network. In this study, the proposed codeword, which integrated time and spectral (wavelength) domain, is constructed as the same prime code sequence and therefore is referred as two-dimension (2-D) optical codes. Importantly, for the proposed broadband light source (BLS), the total number of available wavelengths is partitioned into the different groups G based on the M-sequence code length. Every group is referred as hopping pattern and characterized by the FSR interval of AWG router. To improve the prime-hop code (PHC) and modified prime-hop code (MPHC) of 2-D OCDMA system with cascading one additional AWG router, the cardinality of proposed scheme is significantly increased by the factor of 15 times under the optimum arrangement for group hopping number of G=7. Moreover, the correlation property and bit error rate (BER) of proposed scheme is evaluated and the result reveals that the BER of proposed scheme is better than MPHC and PHC.

articleTitle: Performance investigation of M/G/1/K-based IEEE802.11e EDCA under non-saturation and saturation conditions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The IEEE 802.11e network provides different with QoS (quality of service) guarantee for different traffic streams. The Enhanced Distributed Channel Access(EDCA) in IEEE 802.11e MAC protocol is proposed to support prioritized QoS on the basis of the Distributed Coordination Function(DCF) in IEEE 802.11. We first build a new network analysis model for the EDCA. The model takes into account both the idle state that represents that there are no packets to be transmitted and differentiation based on different AIFS-value for different traffic. We can use the signal transfer function of the generalized state transition diagram to derive a probability distribution of the MAC layer service time and analyze the performance of EDCA from a non-saturated channel to a saturated medium by using M/G/l/K queuing model. The proposed model is calculated numerically and validated against simulation results, we observed a good match between the analytical model and simulation which conforms the veracity of proposed model. Simulation and theoretical results show that despite providing prioritized QoS, the EDCA still can not support strict QoS for real-time application like voice and video unless network works in the non-saturation case. On the other hand, it is inevitable that there is unfairness of channel access to prioritized traffic due to EDCA.

articleTitle: An active index diffusion scheme for multilayer unstructured peer-to-peer networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In order to improve the scalability and reduce the traffic of Gnutella-like unstructured peer-to-peer networks, index caching and controlled flooding mechanisms had been discussed in recent years. Some of them had modified the network architecture and adapted existing search methods for their mechanisms. Although the traffic of querying popular keywords could be reduced by using index caching mechanisms, the cached indices have too redundant replications in the whole network. We propose a multiplayer index diffusion scheme which actively diffuses the indices in the network and groups indices according to their request rate. The peers of the group that have indices with higher request rate will be placed in layers that receive queries earlier. Simulation studies show that the proposed approach can keep a high success query rate as well as reduce the flooding size.

articleTitle: [Conference front matter]
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Conference proceedings front matter may contain various advertisements, welcome messages, committee or program information, and other miscellaneous conference information. This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Contents of Proceedings of ICCCAS 2007
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Presents the table of contents for the proceedings of the 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and fairness policy analysis of Register Insertion Ring
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Resilient packet ring (RPR) provides higher bandwidth utilization than other ring technologies. Bandwidth utilization and fairness policy are very important for RPR. RPR can be regarded as Register Insertion Ring (RIR). For more generality, we developed a primary bandwidth model of RIR and analysed its bandwidth utilization and fairness policy. The results show that: The dual-ring have the advantage of bandwidth utilization effective over single ring. RIR has maximum throughput in “Ring” traffic pattern, and has no advantages than conventional rings in “Star” traffic pattern. RIR has a little advantage over conventional rings in “Balance Mesh” traffic pattern using station-based fairness policy, and more advantage using flow-based fairness policy. And flow-based fairness is the optimum policy for RIR to achieve maximum throughput.

articleTitle: A Fast Nonlinear Timing Analysis Method for Nanometer Technologies
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Timing analysis Method needs to be both accurate and efficient, especially for the submicron VLSI circuit designs. In this paper, a fast high-accuracy timing analysis method is presented. Nonlinear Current-based cell delay model is utilized, which can achieve the goal of accurate nanometer timing including voltage and temperature variation. At the same time, we choose a quick reduced-order network model to keep this method efficient. Experimental results in a 90nm technology show that the delays are accurately estimated, while the running time and memory cost is at a low level.

articleTitle: Multiple Biometric Recognition System with the Function of Real-time Display
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we describe the multiple biometric recognition system based on 32 bit floating-point digital signal processor (DSP) and field programmable gates array (FPGA). In addition, it has the function of real-time display, which can help the users easily capture the perfect image that they need. Different from other platforms of using DSP and FPGA, we have two kinds of parallel bus interfaces between them, the EMIF and HPI interface. With the help of the Hardware Description Language (HDL) Verilog HDL, we make it true that the DPS and FPGA can co-process the matching algorithms. Comparing with the matching time that processes only by the DSP, the co-processing is more efficient than the processing only by one processor. Besides, we leave several parallel and series interfaces in our board for the future use. Therefore, our system can be applied to many different digital signal processing domains and provide them an excellent computing platform.

articleTitle: Resonating photoconductive microwave switches for reconfigurable antenna system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Photoconductive microwave switches with inline-embedded resonating filter for the application in reconfigurable antenna systems are presented. The resonating filters are used to block microwave signals under the dark state so that it can effectively improve the isolation of the devices. These novel switches are numerically simulated by commercial software and results show that the proposed switches have great improvement of the isolation by 20dB than the photoconductive microstrip switches previously reported. The maximum isolation obtained at X band can be up to 53dB.

articleTitle: Mining Co-regulated Genes Using Association Rules Combined with Hash-tree and Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Genes with similar patterns of mRNA expression and similar functions are likely to be regulated via the same mechanisms. This work is based on Association Rules, combined with Hash-tree and Genetic Algorithm to mine co-regulated genes from yeast genome dataset by generating lots of co-regulated rules. The computer experiments verified the effectiveness of the proposed method. Comparing with the GO database, the results showed that some important relationships between the genes in function, component or process are found by our method. Some genes without annotation yet are also inferred to have similar functions with those annotated genes in same rule.

articleTitle: A novel micro-payment scheme for M-commerce based on self-renewal hash chains
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: JI et al improved R. Revest's PayWord scheme based on hash chains and proposed a micro-payment scheme which had better security and fairness, but the scheme did not solve the problems of user's malicious overdraft and its executive timeliness. Furthermore its efficiency and security was restricted by the inherent shortcoming of conventional hash chains (CHC). The paper proposes a micro-payment scheme based on self-renewal hash chains scheme (SRHC). The analysis results show that the proposed scheme not only solves the problems existed in JI's scheme, but also has better features on security, efficiency and fairness. The novel scheme fits scenario of repeated micro-payment such as information commodity between a mobile user and a fixed service provider.

articleTitle: MTIM for IEEE 802.11 DCF power saving mode
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN, after the transmission of each beacon frame, there will be a large number of stations in power saving mode (PS mode, PSM) trying to send power saving poll (PS-Poll) frames to contend the right to receive the buffered downlink packets. However, excessive contention results in higher collision probability, higher power consumption and lower throughput than usual. To solve this problem, we propose a downlink access scheme which modifies the traffic indication map (TIM) fields in beacon frames to enhance the control ability of access point (AP). This scheme which can be used in both the basic access scheme and the access scheme with RTS/CTS enables AP to constrain the number of stations in contention to be an optimal number. Furthermore, the proposed MTIM scheme provides a convenient way for quality of service (QoS) differentiation by limiting the PS-Poll transmitting of stations with lower priority. Simulation results provided in this paper prove the performance improvement.

articleTitle: A Sequential Circuit Partitioning Algorithm for Dynamically Reconfigurable FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a sequential circuit partitioning algorithm to minimize the number of registers for dynamically reconfigurable FPGAs. The algorithm is performed on our specific graph model and divided into two phases: 1) the labeling phase and 2) the minimizing cost phase. We first use as soon as possible and as late as possible algorithms to assign nodes so that the precedence constraints are satisfied. Then, some nodes are adjusted or replicated according to several proposed methods to minimize the number of registers. Experimental results demonstrate the effectives of our algorithms.

articleTitle: Joint beamforming with space-time block coding for multi-antenna communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A downlink transmit scheme joint beamforming (BF) with space-time block coding (STBC) is presented for multi-antenna communications. The proposed scheme first uses the equivalent scaled additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel induced by STBC to yield the closed-form expression of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver. Then based on the symbol error rate (SER) upper bound as design criterion, an optimal beamformer is developed, which is turned out to be an eigen-beamformer with proper power allocation among the multiple beams. Finally, some representative computer simulation results demonstrate that the proposed transmit scheme outperforms not only the conventional STBC, but also the other existing related strategies.

articleTitle: Study of Digital Video Interface (DVI) Architecture Design in Computer System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: in computer system, some digital display devices often are adopted. At this time if still select conventional analog interface, digital signal from person computer (PC) need be switched twice by D/A and A/D, lost of video signal will emerge, so a kind of new interface, DVI technology often need be studied. Combining with real project, this paper introduces the detailed developing methods of Digital Video Interface (DVI) transmitter and receiver in computer Systems. These include the arranging of the architecture of Digital Video Interface (DVI) transmitter and receiver, the design of over-sampler, elasticity buffer, clock recovery circuit, and data recovery circuits, in addition selecting and designing of Phase Frequency Detector (PFD), Charge Pump (CP) and Loop Filter (LF), and Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO) in hardware system were discussed in detail. These can offer a kind of reference method for developing of Digital Video Interface (DVI) transmitter and receiver hardware architecture in computer Systems.

articleTitle: Resonating photoconductive microwave switches for reconfigurable antenna system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Photoconductive microwave switches with inline-embedded resonating filter for the application in reconfigurable antenna systems are presented. The resonating filters are used to block microwave signals under the dark state so that it can effectively improve the isolation of the devices. These novel switches are numerically simulated by commercial software and results show that the proposed switches have great improvement of the isolation by 20dB than the photoconductive microstrip switches previously reported. The maximum isolation obtained at X band can be up to 53dB.

articleTitle: Aggregated self-similar wireless traffic properties analyses based on Sup-FRPP model
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, Superposition Fractal Renewal Point Process (Sup-FRPP) is applied to analyze the average arrival rate, Hurst parameter and the fractality start-time of the aggregated self-similar traffic. Simulation results demonstrate that the aggregated multiple self-similar traffic streams also exhibits self-similarity, which actually intensifies rather than diminishes burstiness of single self-similar traffic stream. The burstiness can have detrimental effects on the network performance. Thus these results are very useful for forecasting network traffic variation, optimizing bandwidth allocation and guaranteeing network Quality of Service (QoS).

articleTitle: A kind of Strategy Based on Adaptive Fuzzy Control and its Application to Aero Engine Turbine Power
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Aero engine turbine power is a typical nonlinear system with characters of time-variable, strong interruption, uncertainty and model complication. It is difficult to achieve good effects by traditional control methods. Adaptive stable control of aero engine power generation system is realized by using adaptive fuzzy control strategy based on variable domain. In this paper, the basic structure of adaptive fuzzy controller based on variable domain is elaborated at firstly, and then the adaptive fuzzy controller is designed by utilizing the adjustability of the contraction-expansion factor a on line and the adaptive law of factor alpha, finally, by the field tests and trial production, it is proved that the control scheme is reliable and effective.

articleTitle: Iterative detection for differential decode-and-forward cooperative communication
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, We proposed an iterative method to estimate the instantaneous probability of error (IPE) and carry maximum likelihood (ML) detection for differential decode-and-forward (DDF) transmission scheme of two-user cooperative communication system. With this method, the transmission of source-to-relay SNR from relay to destination, which is necessary in the previous scheme [4], is not required. The bit error rate (BER) performance is better than previous scheme [4] which is based on average probability of error (APE)[3].

articleTitle: Controlling Projective Synchronization in Two Coupled Fractional Order Chen Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposed a method to achieve projective synchronization of two fractional order Chen systems. First, construct the fractional order Chen system's corresponding approximation integer order system. Then, a control method based on a partially linear decomposition and negative feedback of state errors was utilized on the integer order system. Numerical simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed method..

articleTitle: A nested multistage adaptive beamformer for wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A multistage adaptive beamformer for wireless communications is proposed. The beamformer adopts a novel nested system architecture to reduce the system complexity and to achieve the system optimization which is carried out independently at each stage. It is shown that this method attains an improved performance in comparison to another competitive method.

articleTitle: Iterative detection for differential decode-and-forward cooperative communication
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, We proposed an iterative method to estimate the instantaneous probability of error (IPE) and carry maximum likelihood (ML) detection for differential decode-and-forward (DDF) transmission scheme of two-user cooperative communication system. With this method, the transmission of source-to-relay SNR from relay to destination, which is necessary in the previous scheme [4], is not required. The bit error rate (BER) performance is better than previous scheme [4] which is based on average probability of error (APE)[3].

articleTitle: A novel transfer protocol for reputation sharing on P2P networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In recent years, the polling protocol has been adopted to identify reliable resource providers and distribute sharing reputation values among peers in Peer-to-Peer overlay network. In this paper, security vulnerabilities of the polling protocols in the Gnutella-like P2P networks were analyzed, and Shamir threshold ideas were adopted to build a nearly security encryption of the reputation value. The creative features of the approach lie in the distribution of division of reputation values and selection of multi-path based on the special characteristic of reputation values as evaluation. Furthermore, we analyzed and discussed the robustness and security of our protocol, and it shows that it is resistant to several known attacks and can effectively solve the possible threat generated by the Gnutella protocol.

articleTitle: Hamming Distance and Normalization Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Hamming distance and normalization are important in many digital signal processing algorithms apart from multiply and multiply-accumulate operations. These operations are time consuming unless complex hardware is included, increasing power consumption and latency. This paper proposes a design based on a compressor circuit implemented by pass-transistor logic to perform both the Hamming distance and normalization functions on the same circuit for a general DSP. This enables a significant reduction in the number of transistors without sacrificing the performance or incurring the power penalty compared to the earlier designs which implemented the functions separately.

articleTitle: Chaotic Synchronization of a Fractional Neuron Network System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Chaos in a fractional-order neuron network system is illustrated. Chaotic synchronization system for a fractional-order neuron network system is constructed. The theoretic analyses are given by Laplace transformation theory, the bifurcation graph with respect to coupled parameter is presented, and the numerical experiments are presented. The study shows that the chaos in such fractional-order neuron networks could be synchronized.

articleTitle: A joint channel estimation and detection algorithm for OFDM systems with short Cyclic Prefix
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Combined with the matrix expression of OFDM system, a joint channel estimation and detection algorithm for short Cyclic Prefix (CP) OFDM system is proposed. The proposed algorithm uses the predicted channel response and last detected data symbol provided by the WLMS algorithm to remove the interblock interference (IBI). At the same time, to reduce the complexity of the proposed algorithm, we present an iterative interference cancellation algorithm which eliminates the sub-carrier interference of short CP-OFDM system. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves its reliable channel estimation and data detection. Compared with long CP-OFDM systems, the system efficiency is improved and the system performance loss is little.

articleTitle: Joint beamforming with space-time block coding for multi-antenna communications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A downlink transmit scheme joint beamforming (BF) with space-time block coding (STBC) is presented for multi-antenna communications. The proposed scheme first uses the equivalent scaled additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel induced by STBC to yield the closed-form expression of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver. Then based on the symbol error rate (SER) upper bound as design criterion, an optimal beamformer is developed, which is turned out to be an eigen-beamformer with proper power allocation among the multiple beams. Finally, some representative computer simulation results demonstrate that the proposed transmit scheme outperforms not only the conventional STBC, but also the other existing related strategies.

articleTitle: A write-in electronic voting scheme based on ring signature
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We present a new e-voting scheme based on ring signature that satisfies three major properties: (1) "Everlasting anonymity" or unconditional voter-indistinguishability: even a computationally unbounded party does not gain any information about individual votes anytime, even after tally or in future. This is the first explicitly unconditional privacy discussion in e-voting schemes. (2)Uniform interface of ballots: it has no restriction on the form of ballots: "yes/no", k-out-of-m or adding their own candidates, all of which can be realized under uniform interface. (3)High-efficiency: the symmetric cryptography, which is fast and efficient, and the voting phase is only one-round. In addition, our scheme effectively prevents CTF cheating and overcomes the disadvantage in most existed solutions, which excessively dependent on the organization of voting. It not only protects benefits of voters, but also assures the fairness of voting, and can be suitable to all kinds' scales of electronic voting.

articleTitle: High-Speed Continuous Time Digitizer Using a Two-Level Multiphase Sampling Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the new architecture of a high-speed continuous time digitizer has been proposed. With the aid of a two-level multiphase sampling technique, the time digitizer can use only 16 delay cells and DFFs to perform the flash-type conversion of 64-stage interpolation. The time digitizer can obtain 78 ps resolution with a reference frequency running at 200 MHz. The continuous input clock frequency can be up to 250 MHz. The layout area occupies 1.08 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A novel clock multiplier is also introduced to provide multiphase generation with frequency output range within 640 MHz ~1.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A SPICE-Oriented Nonexistence Test for DC Solutions of Nonlinear Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: As a powerful computational test for nonexistence of a DC solution of a nonlinear circuit, the LP test is well-known. This test is useful for finding all solutions of nonlinear circuits; it is also useful for verifying the nonexistence of a DC operating point in a given region where operating points should not exist. However, the LP test has not been widely used in practical circuit simulation because the programming is not easy for non-experts or beginners. In this paper, we propose a new LP test that can be easily implemented on SPICE without programming. The proposed test is useful because we can easily check the nonexistence of a solution using SPICE only.

articleTitle: Pilot-aided CFO estimation in clipped OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Pilot-aided carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation is a promising CFO estimation technique in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system. However, in a clipped OFDM system, the clipping noise will distort the pilot tones, so as to degrade the CFO estimation performance. To alleviate this problem, in this paper, a new technique is proposed to reduce the influence of the clipping noise on pilot-aided CFO estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed technique can effectively improve the CFO estimation performance in clipped OFDM system.

articleTitle: Dual Digital Watermarking Used in Product Casing
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, it is proposed an invisible dual digital watermarking scheme based on DCT domain, which can be used in the product casing. By embedding fragile and robust watermark simultaneously, the scheme can both prevent the product from forgery and take the information of its serial number.

articleTitle: Exponential Stabilization for Impulsive Control of T-S Fuzzy Systems with Small Delays
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper studies Takagi-Sugeno(T-S) fuzzy model with impulsive effects and small delays and deals with a hybrid impulsive and switched controller design. Using the method of Lyapunov functions, we present globally exponential stability theorem of Takagi-Sugeno(T-S) fuzzy model-based impulsive control system with small delays.

articleTitle: An Effective Implementation of the Nonlinear Homotopy Method for MOS Transistor Circuits Based on SPICE3
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Homotopy methods are attractive for finding DC operating points of nonlinear circuits due to its global convergence in principle. In this paper, the homotopy method using a nonlinear auxiliary function is described and implemented for MOS transistor circuits. The implementation is based on the SPICE3 simulator and employs the initial solution and BDF (backward differentiation formula) solution curve-tracing algorithms. The simulation results demonstrate the efficiency, which are compared with the ATANSH-based homotopy method.

articleTitle: Rich Dynamics in a Small Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper shows that rich dynamics can take place in a simple three dimensional continuous-time Hopfield neural network with its connection matrix satisfying Dale's rule. In order to get a detailed picture of the complex dynamics, chaos and transient chaos are also studied by virtue of topological horseshoe theory.

articleTitle: A Novel Speaker Change Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: To cope with the problem of speaker voice change detection, a novel speaker change detection algorithm is proposed in this paper. The new algorithm is developed based on traditional BIC algorithm in order to choose the voice segmentation point firstly, and then analyze the BIC change trend to decide which point is the real speaker voice change point. To compare with the normal BIC detection algorithm, the precision and recall rate of this new one is improved a lot. And also the new one has lower computational complexity compared with the traditional one.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Several FIR Fractional Delay Filters in Element-Interpolation DPCA
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Element-interpolation DPCA (Displaced Phase Center Antenna) employs a fractional delay filter to get good GMTI(Ground Moving Target Indication) performance while conventional DPCA conditions cannot be met. Its GMTI performance seriously depends on the adopted filter. This paper evaluates 4 fractional delay filters in element-interpolation DPCA, and provides guidelines for choosing an appropriate filter to get best GMTI performance (ICCCAS'07).

articleTitle: A dynamic channel estimation in MIMO communication system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Channel estimation is essential in digital communication. In MIMO transmission it is augmented by the need of transceiver with an equalizing sequence in each symbol. And the non-frequency and stationary fading channel is a prerequisite for MIMO transmission in state-of -art, that's the why MIMO technique is mainly used as indoor communication. In this paper we propose to use an adaptive multiple dimensional support vector regressor (AM-SVR) for estimating MIMO communication channels because of the good generalization properties the SVR presents for short training sequences. Instead of using quadratic programming (QP) procedures for solving the M-SVR, as is usually done, we present an iterative re-weighted least squares procedure for attaining the M-SVR solution, because it is a procedure simple to implement and allows a recursive formulation that is impossible for QP schemes. We analyze the performance of the proposed algorithm using computer simulations in mobile MIMO communication scenarios.

articleTitle: The Total Dose Radiation Hardened MOSFET with Good High-temperatue Performance
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Total dose radiation hardened partial silicon-on-insulator (PSOI) MOSFET structure is proposed in this paper. Radiation effects of SOI and PSOI MOSFET are discussed and compared. Simulation results show that the subthreshold performance of SOI MOSFET is significantly deteriorated even under low radiation dose. But the total dose radiation tolerance of PSOI MOSFET is superior to its conventional SOI counterpart under the same radiation dose. Additionally, the influence of transistor's physical parameters on total dose radiation is analyzed. The tolerance is enhanced with the increase of the PSOI silicon window length when the devices are under high total dose conditions. Furthermore, PSOI MOSFET performs better than that of SOI MOSFET at high temperature under harsh radiation condition.

articleTitle: Rough Set-based Intelligent Agent Grid Data Management
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposed an intelligent agent grid data management method based on rough set. It can effectively classify data based on attributes reduction in rough set. After obtaining the classified data sets, it dispatches a collection of agents to coordinate a user job over grid computing to process the certain data sets. Our method can well resolve the main problems exist in grid data management. The experimental results indicates our proposed approach can reduce about sixteen percent implement time comparing to general grid data management without rough set classification.

articleTitle: Multi-party fair exchange protocol with an Off-line Semi-Trust Third Party
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A multi-party fair exchange protocol is a cryptographic protocol allowing several parties to exchange electronic items in such a way that everyone gives an item away if and only if it receives an item in return. In this paper, we present a new multi-party fair exchange protocol with an Off-line Semi-Trust Third Party (OSTTP). The new protocol can ensure strong fairness and the OSTTP can't get the exchanged secrets without conspiring with any participants.

articleTitle: Study on the Dual Camera Photogrammetry and Signal Process in Photoelectric Landing Guidance System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we designed a photoelectric guidance system for helicopter landing and recovery. Two infrared CCD cameras were used to image the four beacons lighted by semiconductor lasers on both sides of the helicopter. The beacon position and attitude were extracted by image process and target identification. Using the dual camera photogrammetry(DCP) model established, the real-time helicopter coordinates were calculated relative to the landing point. Using the high performance DSP system, two channel of image signal were collected, detected and tracked in real time and the experimental results were displayed. The hardware-in-the-loop experiment shows that the measurement accuracy of distance can reach plusmn5 cm and the measurement accuracy of angle can reach plusmn3degin the guidance system. The errors meet the accuracy requirements of safe landing for helicopters.

articleTitle: Password authenticated key agreement with smart cards for remote systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a password authenticated key agreement scheme for remote systems. This scheme adopts smart cards and is built on bilinear pairings. It employs Diffie-Hellman key exchange to achieve perfect forward security. Furthermore, the proposed scheme allows registered users to update their passwords freely without any assistance from the remote system.

articleTitle: The Algorithm of Iris Image Quality Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we judge whether an iris image has quality problem from two aspects. On one hand, we analyze the higher spatial frequency sub-band image of the original iris normalization image and determine whether this image has eyelid and lash occlusion problem according to the number of high value pixels. On the other hand, we determine whether an iris image is clear enough though computing the variance of the wavelet coefficients. Through our experiments, this algorithm is proved to be universal and efficient.

articleTitle: Rotational-invariance code design for the system of TCM_CPM
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Continuous phase modulation (CPM) is an attractive technique for digital communication, with the development of the trellis coded modulation (TCM), the combination of TCM and CPM is largely applied to improve the performance of MCPM. However, the combination of TCM and CPM cannot utilize unattached differential encoding simply to solve the problem that phase offset caused. As a result, a rotational-invariance system of TCM_CPM is needed to solve the problem. This paper based on the Corneliu Eugen D.Sterian's design of the rotational-invariance TCM_QPSK (QPSK: quad phase shift keying) and TCM_QAM (QAM: quadrature amplitude modulation am), considered the characteristic of CPM, and made a rotational-invariance code design for the system of TCM_CPM, which ensure the system invariant to rotations of the signal constellation by symmetry angles. We did the simulation of rotational-invariance system of 32 states 8CPM and 4CPM TCM_CPM, with pi/4 rotational-invariance.

articleTitle: A Power Electronic Switching Circuit for a HTS Resonantor
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An electronic switch prototype has been developed for control of a high temperature superconductor (HTS) R-C-L series resonant device. The device built mainly consists of an electronic power switch with potential use of a high Q HTS inductor. In practice electrical resistance in the circuit, which mainly comes from the inductor, limits the voltages that can be achieved. Consequently an inductor with low resistance is required to achieve high voltage generation and a higher current. This paper will describe the prototype device, and the high voltage generation method.

articleTitle: A new two dimensional analytical breakdown model of SOI RESURF devices
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a new breakdown model of SOI RESURF devices is proposed based on solving 2-D Poisson equation. The approach explores the physical insights of the lateral and vertical breakdowns for both of the completely and incompletely depleted drift regions. Analytical 2-D electrostatic potential and electric fields distributions are compared with the simulating results by MEDICI, The impacts of the geometry parameters on the breakdown voltage are also investigated by the analytical model and numerical simulation. A well agreement between the analytical and simulating results proofs the availability of the model. Finally, as a further experimental verification, LDMOS with a breakdown voltage of 220V was fabricated on a bonding SOI wafer with a top silicon thickness of 3.0μm and a buried oxide thickness of 1.5μm.

articleTitle: A New Method of Combined Classifier Design Based on Fuzzy Integral and Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: To make the modulation classification system more suitable for signals in a wide range of signal noise rate (SNR), a novel method of designing combined classifier based on fuzzy integral and multi-class support vector machines (MSVM) is presented in this paper. The method employs multi-class support vector machines classifiers and fuzzy integral to improve recognition reliability. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed combined classifier has high recognition rate with large variation range of SNR (success rates are over 98.2% when SNR is not lower than 5dB).

articleTitle: A New Speech Source Locating System Using Orthocenter Locating Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The speech source locating technology using orthocenter locating algorithm has been researched and a far-field signal model based on microphone array is obtained. As the single cross-array is too small to estimate the position, it's only used to detection bearings. So a new locating algorithm is presented in this paper. It is the first time to use this locating algorithm in practical speech source locating system. In this paper, three cross-arrays are used to form a triangle-array which is in big size. Cross-array is the sub-array, and triangle-array is the main-array. To each cross-array, we use the modified MUSIC (multiple signal classification) algorithm to estimate DOA (direction of arrival). This algorithm utilizes two dimensional searching for spectrum peak to get the plane angle and the polar angle. With the bearing results of sub-arrays, main-array confirms a point in the triangle enclosed by locating lines as the target position. The point is the orthocenter of the enclosed triangle. The results of the simulation prove that this algorithm can restrain noise, and improve the performance of the speech source locating system.

articleTitle: Iris-based remote user authentication scheme using smart cards
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A remote user authentication scheme based on the algorithm of Awasthi and Lal is proposed. The proposed scheme uses an iris-based biometric cryptographic technique to overcome the difficulty of managing security parameters in the Awasthi and Lal scheme. By combining remote user authentication and iris-based biometric cryptography, the proposed scheme achieves the security strength of the Awasthi and Lal scheme and at the same time addresses the issue of management of secret data of that scheme.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm of Detecting Circular Edge Based on Multiresolution Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In order to accelerate the speed of traditional Hough Transform of detecting and locating the circular object in an image, a new approach has been introduced in this paper which is based on multiresolution wavelet transform. By utilizing odd order Bspline wavelet function, the image dimension can be reduced; the gradient and tangent angle of the image pixels could be calculated; and the image edges can be extracted as well. Since tangent angles of an image have been calculated, the dimension of parameter space in Hough Transform also reduces. Therefore, after preprocessing the original image by means of Bspline wavelet Transform, we can detect the circular object fast and precisely through improved algorithm of improved Hough Transform. By analyzing the process of this algorithm, we can find that the computation of the algorithm can decrease in proportion to the exponential function of image scale. Finally, we demonstrate our method through experiment test which is realized by programming on matlab.

articleTitle: Research on spam filtering technology using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Support Vector Machine is a novel machine learning method based on statistical learning theory, and it has been successfully applied to spam filtering system. This paper gives a research to Mail-head Character Categorization using Support Vector Machine(SVM).A total of 106 features were extracted and the filtering performance is good. And the training time is substantially reduced because of the lower dimensional feature space. Finally we implement an automatic Mail-head Character Categorization system, and it also gives the test results.

articleTitle: A triple-controlled DDS-based PLL for 3 to 4 GHz frequency synthesis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a triple-controlled direct digital synthesis (DDS)-based phase-locked loop (PLL) for 3 to 4 GHz frequency synthesis is presented. The architecture has the merits of low spurs, a fast switching speed and high frequency resolution. It corrects the output of DDS and changes the division ratios of two variable frequency dividers in PLL to avoid high level spurs falling in the loop bandwidth of PLL. The additional DAC output is added to the output of the loop filter to drive the VCO. It provides the PLL with a fast switching speed. Experiment and measurement results showed that this type of frequency synthesizer architecture has better performance than conventional PLL and can be used in most applications of frequency synthesis.

articleTitle: A novel Position Code Parallel Combinatory Spread Spectrum communication system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel Position Code Parallel Combinatory Spread Spectrum (PC/PC/SS) communication system. PC/PC/SS system can be designed to have higher data transmission capability, even several times compared to ordinary PC/SS system on Gaussian channel. In the ordinary PC/SS system, multip1e pseudo-noise (PN) sequences are simultaneously transmitted out of a pre-assigned spreading sequence set. In the proposed system, modulation of Position Code is applied to the starting position of each simultaneously transmitting PN sequences. The symbol error rate and average bit error rate are analyzed to evaluate the performance of the proposed systems. Furthermore, PC/PC/SS system has excellent secret property than PC/SS and M-ary/SS communication systems.

articleTitle: DC Tolerance Analysis of Nonlinear Circuits Using Set-Valued Functions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the tolerance analysis of electronic circuits, the concept of set-valued function is often useful. In this paper, an efficient algorithm is proposed for finding all solution sets of nonlinear resistive circuits described by systems of nonlinear equations containing set-valued functions termed piecewise-trapezoidal functions. By numerical examples, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified from various viewpoints. It is also shown that the proposed algorithm could find all solution regions to a system of 1000 piecewise-trapezoidal equations in practical computation time.

articleTitle: Reliability-based subpacket transmission for hybrid ARQ with LDPC codes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An irregular LDPC coded sub-packet hybrid ARQ (HARQ) scheme based on instantaneous reliability is presented for selection and retransmission. Reliability-based (RB) HARQ was initially proposed for Turbo coded case with iterative decoding, whereas for irregular LDPC coded scenario, a degree distribution based (DDB) retransmission strategy was presented that the nodes with large degree have higher retransmission priority in [10]. In this paper, we focus on the improved approach to segment and select sub-packets according to instantaneous reliability for potential throughput performance enhancement. Numeral results with link level simulation demonstrate that a significant throughput gain is realized by setting suitable length of sub-packets for reliability based retransmission than DDB scheme.

articleTitle: Study on Theory and Key Technologies of Full Digital SPWM Implementation for Three-Level Neutral Point Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The digital realization theory and key technologies of Multi-level SPWM scheme implementation for the three-level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) inverter is presented. The digital asymmetrical regular sampling principle of SPWM is realized with only a single FPGA chip LFEC10 from LATTICE Inc. and the programming language is Very High Speed Integrated Circuit Hardware Description Language (VHDL). This full digital circuit can provide an effective, flexible, and safe solution for high-power inverts. At last, some simulation and experimental results have been presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A More General Form of Apriori and Its Application in Clustering Security Events
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Due to its excellent performance, Apriori is frequently adopted to discover frequent itemsets, from which strong association rules can be easily generated, from among massive amounts of transactional or relational data. In this paper, Apriori is reconsidered with a more abstract perspective of data space, and a more general form of the algorithm is proposed. As is shown in this paper, the newly proposed form of the algorithm can be effectively applied to more situations in which its primitive form does not work. The more general form of Apriori is successfully applied to the problem of clustering security events organized in a hierarchical manner, which illustrates its usefulness.

articleTitle: Design of the High-powered Clutter Suppression System Based on ADSP-TS203
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The paper studies the design to implement moving target indication (MTI) and moving target detection (MTD) based on a piece of ADSP-TS203. Digital signal processor (DSP) provides great flexibility for the design of the software. After pulse compression, the radar echoes including clutter, noise and targets are transmitted to DSP for MTI and MTD. The system mainly adopts the arithmetic of three-pulse elimination to realize MTI. MTD can be completed by using a narrow-band-Doppler-filter group in frequency domain. At last, it's verified that this system can restrain clutter and distinguish the targets effectively, which has been tested on the hardware. Meanwhile, the improvement factor is also improved. The system can be widely used in radar signal processing.

articleTitle: MMAR:A deadlock recovery-based fault tolerant routing algorithm for mesh/torus networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In direct networks, such as mesh and torus, the switching capacity will increase as the number of components increase. But the fault probability of the network also increases with the increasing of components. This paper proposes a novel fault-tolerant algorithm, named as minimal misrouted adaptive routing (MMAR) which is based on true fully adaptive routing algorithm and deadlock recovery mechanism. Due to the high adaptability, MMAR can accommodate arbitrary shaped fault models using minimal number of virtual channels in each physical link. When encountering concave fault models, MMAR minimizes the length of the misrouted path by avoiding routing the message into the irrespective holes. Simulation results show that MMAR can work efficiently and achieve favorable performance.

articleTitle: An improved analog AGC for TD-SCDMA receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Time Division-Synchronous CDMA (TDSCDMA) uses time division duplex (TDD) for unsymmetrical data rate transmission, making conventional closed-loop automatic gain control (AGC) schemes impractical for TDSCDMA receiver. An improved analog AGC algorithm used in TD-SCDMA receiver is presented, the general model is given and an equivalent linear system is proposed. Finally, the simulation and test results are given. The validity of the algorithm is verified by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: An integration of polyphase filter and polyphase mixer architecture for high-speed DDC
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a new architecture is proposed for high-speed Digital Down Conversion (DDC) for communication signal processing. The proposed architecture integrates conventional Polyphase Filter with Polyphase Mixer (PFPM) for decimation in DDC. The PFPM architecture decreases both the rate of the mixer and filter and can process the signals with a very high sample rate, which cannot be realistically implement in conventional DDC in a General Purpose Processor (GPP) such as Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or Digital Signal Processor (DSP). Simulation and experiment have been done to verify the availability of the PFPM architecture. These results show that the proposed PFPM architecture reduces the operation rate of the mixer and well agrees with the conventional DDC architecture.

articleTitle: Transmission adaptation for MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Different transmission schemes have different diversity and multiplexing tradeoff characters. Adjusting MIMO transmission scheme according to channel quality indicator (CQI) or channel state information will improve system performance. This paper proposes a new transmission adaptation solution depending on two-dimensional channel quality indicators with the aim to enhance system throughput performance. This is realized by using different transmission schemes, which support different data streams. We first implement our algorithm in single carrier MIMO system and then extend it to MIMO-OFDM system with practical correlation scenario. Simulation results show significant throughput gain compared to conventional fixed transmission schemes and conventional adaptation technique.

articleTitle: Diagonal Loading Techniques to Relax Sample Support Requirement in Airborne Bistatic STAP
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we concentrate on the employment of diagonal loading to relax sample size requirement of airborne bistatic STAP. Due to the independent motion effects of the receiver and transmitter, bistatic clutter generally appears more severely nonstationary in the range dimension than the counterpart of monostatic system. This leads to the shortage of IID training data samples and inadequate estimation of the clutter-plus-noise covariance matrix for bistatic STAP, which greatly degrades the performance of bistatic STAP. In this work, we first make a comparison of sample support in different bistatic scenarios and then propose to further abate the required sample support by combining the diagonal loading techniques with the reduced-dimension STAP algorithm. Simulation results manifest that the satisfying performance of bistatic STAP can be obtained by using the proposed method in the bistatic geometries where the training data is extremely insufficient.

articleTitle: An improved analog AGC for TD-SCDMA receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The Time Division-Synchronous CDMA (TDSCDMA) uses time division duplex (TDD) for unsymmetrical data rate transmission, making conventional closed-loop automatic gain control (AGC) schemes impractical for TDSCDMA receiver. An improved analog AGC algorithm used in TD-SCDMA receiver is presented, the general model is given and an equivalent linear system is proposed. Finally, the simulation and test results are given. The validity of the algorithm is verified by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A novel blind channel estimation method for MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Channel estimation method is a key issue in MIMO system. In recent years, a lot of papers on subspace(SS)-based blind channel estimation have been published, and in this paper, combining SS method with a space-time coding scheme, we proposed a novel blind channel estimation method in MIMO system. Simulation result demonstrates the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Study and design of intelligent current-sharing controller in excitation power units
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Parallel power rectifier cabinets can increase the capacity of excitation system while may cause serious current unbalance problems among cabinets or thyristors. In this paper, the design of intelligent current-sharing controller (ICSC) based on infineon micro controller unit (MCU) XC164 and field programmable gate array (FPGA) is discussed in detail. The fuzzy self-adaptive PID control algorithm is adopted to slightly adjust the firing pulse for realizing current-sharing among parallel thyristors and thereby among parallel cabinets. The simulation results attest the validity of the design.

articleTitle: Cross-layer energy efficient clustering for heterogeneous wireless sensor networks with renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The clustering Algorithm is a kind of key technique used to reduce energy consumption. It can increase the scalability and lifetime of the networks. Energy-efficient clustering algorithm should be designed for the characteristic of heterogeneous wireless sensor networks. We propose and evaluate a new cross-layer energy efficient clustering (CLEEC) algorithm for heterogeneous wireless sensor networks with renewable energy source. In CLEEC, the cluster heads are elected by probabilities based on cross-layer optimal estimation, considering energy replenishment. The cross-layer optimal estimation uses cross-layer information, such as energy and replenishment rate, to theoretically compute the election probabilities. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that our clustering approach outperforms current important clustering algorithms in the efficiency of prolonging the network lifetime.

articleTitle: Diversity set update algorithm for MDHO in cellular fixed relay networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In cellular fixed relay networks diversity set update is an indispensable procedure in MDHO (macro diversity handover) mode. The paper proposes and compares two update algorithms for relay networks: an algorithm without direction information and a direction assisted algorithm. The average number of updates and the received signal strength are used as criteria for performance. The effects of the parameters in direction assisted algorithm are also well analyzed. The simulation results show that the direction assisted algorithm provides fewer update times and well received signal strength.

articleTitle: A unified model for the 1/f noise induced by threading dislocation in strained-Si pMOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A unified accurate 1/f noise model is developed for the strained-Si pMOSFETs with threading dislocations. With the fluctuations of carrier number and mobility taken into account simultaneously, the deep-submicrometre devices are investigated. The numerical results display that the area of the gate is key factor for the device's noise characteristics and that a critical gate area can be defined to evaluate the effects of the threading dislocations. And the 1/f noise induced by threading dislocation shows different characteristics at three conditions respectively. The unified model is also clearly reveal the physical mechanism of 1/f noise generated from threading dislocation definitely and available for deep-submicrometre device simulation, design and reliability applications.

articleTitle: An ant-like agent based data aggregation routing scheme in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Energy efficiency is a very important criterion for the wireless sensor networks. The technology of data aggregation can be adopted to decrease the power costs of redundancy information and delay time. In this paper, we proposed an optimization data aggregation routing algorithm based on ant colony schema (ACAR) using agent collaboration and migration for wireless sensor networks. A number of ant-like mobile agents traverse the wireless sensor network in search of data aggregation paths between given source-destination node pairs while seeking to fulfill a set of requirements (the path objective) provided by the owner/producer of the agents. Our simulation results show that our algorithms perform well in energy efficient compared with directed diffusion protocol.

articleTitle: Research on Amplitude-Phase Consistency of Power Amplifiers in Transmit/Receive Modules
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the amplitude-phase consistency of power amplifiers in Transmit/Receive(T/R) modules is analyzed, and the main reasons for inconsistency of power amplifiers are discussed, the design considerations that improve the amplitude-phase consistency of power amplifiers are also introduced.

articleTitle: An improved 2-D ESPRIT Method for joint DOA-delay estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: For the purpose of estimating DOAs and delays of multipath signals, a novel improved 2-dimensional (2-D) ESPRIT is proposed. The improved method estimates the joint space-time signal subspace firstly. Then FFT and deconvolution is done to map time delay parameters into frequency phase shifts and a modified joint signal subspace is constructed. At last DOAs and delays are estimated by using rotational invariance property. Compared with traditional 2-D ESPRIT method, the method we proposed here can prevent the correlated noise problem when FFT is done to estimated channel directly. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the improved method.

articleTitle: Modeling the Impact of Input-to-Output Coupling Capacitance on Power Dissipation Estimation in Deep Submicron CMOS Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper modeling the impact of input-to-output coupling capacitance on power dissipation estimation in submicron CMOS circuits is proposed. Compared with conventional methods, the proposed model is much accurate because it considers the impact of the input-to-output capacitance on power dissipation estimation. In addition, the proposed model can estimate the impact of coupling capacitance on serial gates. The experimental results show that the proposed model can obtain an considerable improvement in accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimization of polyphase code based on ambiguity function for MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel character segmentation method of license plate based on quick region marking method and the large-interval-based character locating algorithm. This will enhance the accuracy of the recognition system that aims to read automatically the Chinese license plate. In the proposed methodology, the character region in license plate image is enhanced and binarized in the preprocessing stage, and the whole image is performed by the quick region marking method and the candidate regions of characters are located in the following. Then the final character regions are determined based on the large-interval-based character locating algorithm. Finally, the characters are segmented from original license plate. The proposed method in character segmentation is fast and accurate, and is tolerant to license plate with deformations, rotations, plate frame, rivet, the space mark, and so on. And promising results have been obtained in experiments on Chinese license plates.

articleTitle: Efficient encoding of low-density parity-check codes in chinese digital terrestrial television broadcasting standard
publicationTitle: 2007 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
